사사기-10-1.title: 사사기 10장 1절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-1.exegesis: 51-53. all the men and women, ... gat them up to the top of the tower-- The Canaanite forts were generally mountain fastnesses or keeps, and they often had a strong tower which served as a last refuge. The Assyrian bas-reliefs afford counterparts of the scene here described so vivid and exact, that we might almost suppose them to be representations of the same historic events. The besieged city--the strong tower within--the men and women crowding its battlements--the fire applied to the doors, and even the huge fragments of stone dropping from the hands of one of the garrison on the heads of the assailants, are all well represented to the life--just as they are here described in the narrative of inspired truth [Goss].

사사기-10-2.title: 사사기 10장 2절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 10 Jud 10:1-5 . Tola Judges Israel in Shamir. 1. after Abimelech there arose to defend Israel, Tola-- that is, "to save." Deliverance was necessary as well from intestine usurpation as from foreign aggression. the son of Puah-- He was uncle to Abimelech by the father's side, and consequently brother of Gideon; yet the former was of the tribe of Issachar, while the latter was of Manasseh. They were, most probably, uterine brothers. dwelt in Shamir in mount Ephraim-- As a central place, he made it the seat of government.

사사기-10-4.title: 사사기 10장 4절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-4.exegesis: 3. Jair, a Gileadite-- This judge was a different person from the conqueror of that northeastern territory, and founder of Havoth-jair, or "Jair's villages" ( Nu 32:41 ; De 3:14 ; Jos 13:3 ; 1Ch 2:22 ).
사사기-10-4.theologicalNote: 3. Jair, a Gileadite-- This judge was a different person from the conqueror of that northeastern territory, and founder of Havoth-jair, or "Jair's villages" ( Nu 32:41 ; De 3:14 ; Jos 13:3 ; 1Ch 2:22 ).

사사기-10-5.title: 사사기 10장 5절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-5.exegesis: 4. he had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts-- This is a characteristic trait of Eastern manners in those early times; and the grant of a village to each of his thirty sons was a striking proof of his extensive possessions. His having thirty sons is no conclusive evidence that he had more than one wife, much less that he had more than one at a time. There are instances, in this country, of men having as many children by two successive wives.

사사기-10-7.title: 사사기 10장 7절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-7.exegesis: Jud 10:6-9 . Israel Oppressed by the Philistines and Ammonites. 6. the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord-- This apostasy seems to have exceeded every former one in the grossness and universality of the idolatry practised.
사사기-10-7.theologicalNote: Jud 10:6-9 . Israel Oppressed by the Philistines and Ammonites. 6. the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord-- This apostasy seems to have exceeded every former one in the grossness and universality of the idolatry practised.

사사기-10-8.title: 사사기 10장 8절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-8.exegesis: 7. Philistines, and ... the children of Ammon-- The predatory incursions of these two hostile neighbors were made naturally on the parts of the land respectively contiguous to them. But the Ammonites, animated with the spirit of conquest, carried their arms across the Jordan; so that the central and southern provinces of Canaan were extensively desolated.

사사기-10-11.title: 사사기 10장 11절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-11.exegesis: Jud 10:10-15 . They Cry to God. 10. The children of Israel cried unto the Lord, saying, We have sinned against thee-- The first step of repentance is confession of sin, and the best proof of its sincerity is given by the transgressor, when he mourns not only over the painful consequences which have resulted from his offenses to himself, but over the heinous evil committed against God.

사사기-10-12.exegesis: 11. the Lord said ... Did I not deliver you from the Egyptians-- The circumstances recorded in this and the following verses were not probably made through the high priest, whose duty it was to interpret the will of God.

사사기-10-17.title: 사사기 10장 17절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-17.exegesis: Jud 10:16-18 . They Repent; God Pities Them. 16. they put away the strange gods ... and served the Lord; and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel-- On their abandonment of idolatry and return to purity of worship, God graciously abridged the term of national affliction and restored times of peace.

사사기-10-18.title: 사사기 10장 18절 역사문법적 주해
사사기-10-18.exegesis: 17-18. the children of Ammon were gathered together-- From carrying on guerrilla warfare, the Ammonites proceeded to a continued campaign. Their settled aim was to wrest the whole of the trans-jordanic territory from its actual occupiers. In this great crisis, a general meeting of the Israelitish tribes was held at Mizpeh. This Mizpeh was in eastern Manasseh ( Jos 11:3 ).
